title: Normalized integral reduction tensor comparison preserves signed symmetry
statement: Let D be a finite-field datum, l a prime different from D.p, E a finite-dimensional extension of Q_l, and X a scheme. Let a be a normalized tensor-Hom presentation over the completed coefficient sheaf, s its signed symmetry, n a positive quotient index (exponent n+1), m a normalized ReductionPresentation from a at n, and t a signed symmetry of m.target, as in def-sf-integral-verdier-models and def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models. Assume s.swap and t.swap are natural in both derived inputs. Write F for derived scalar reduction and mu for m.mu. Then for every two ambient derived objects K,L, mu.inv(K,L) followed by F(s.swap(K,L).hom) equals t.swap(FK,FL).hom followed by mu.inv(L,K). There is no dualizing object, Hom comparison, evaluation equation, constructibility or boundedness premise.

proof.text: Choose K-flat representatives P,Q using exists_isKFlatResolutionIndependentCoefficients and essential surjectivity of DerivedCategory.Q. The K-flat reduction counits are invertible. Apply m.normalization in both orders to obtain beta and beta-prime with their scalar-unit formulas and normalization squares, and choose chain swaps sigma,tau from the two SignedSymmetry.representative fields.

Use the proved scalarTensor_hom_ext₂ from ModuleTensorExtensionEquation, transported along the recorded identifications of ordinary scalar extension with sheafified extension of scalars. Combining this with mapBifunctor.hom_ext reduces beta followed by extension(sigma) = tau followed by beta-prime to scalar-unit pure total tensors. The normalization and signed-swap formulas reduce both paths to the same (-1)^(ij) multiple of the image of y tensor x. Naturality and additivity of the ordinary extension unit, and naturality of the degree-equality transports, identify these elements.

Apply DerivedCategory.Q to the chain equality. Naturality of the reduction counit follows by composing its quotient-comparison, homotopy derived-counit and ordinary-extension factor transformations. A categorical cancellation argument combines this naturality, the two normalization squares, the two representative swap squares and naturality of the finite swap, giving the hom-form symmetry square on K-flat representatives. Naturality of mu and of both swaps transports it along the representing isomorphisms to K,L. Cancel mu.hom on both sides to obtain the stated inverse-form equation. Zero complexes and empty schemes require no additional hypotheses in the generator calculation.

lean.statement:
theorem reduction_tensor_symmetry
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E] [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E]
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (a : IntegralHom.TensorPresentation.{u, u} X
      (completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E X D hl))
    (s : SignedSymmetry X (completedIntegralCommRingSheaf l E X D hl) a)
    (hs : ∀ (K L K' L' : Ambient l E X) (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L ⟶ L'),
      a.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom f g) ≫ (s.swap K' L').hom =
        (s.swap K L).hom ≫ a.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom g f))
    (n : ℕ) (m : IntegralHom.ReductionPresentation l E X D hl a n)
    (t : SignedSymmetry X (integralCoefficientCommRingSheaf l E X n) m.target)
    (ht : ∀ (K L K' L' : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionTarget l E X n))
      (f : K ⟶ K') (g : L ⟶ L'),
      m.target.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom f g) ≫ (t.swap K' L').hom =
        (t.swap K L).hom ≫ m.target.tensor.map (Prod.mkHom g f))
    (K L : Ambient l E X) :
    m.mu.inv.app (K, L) ≫
        (scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n).map (s.swap K L).hom =
      (t.swap ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n).obj K)
        ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n).obj L)).hom ≫ m.mu.inv.app (L, K)
